title: Generation of hepato-biliary-pancreatic organoid from human pluripotent stem cells
protocol: Mix Advanced DMEM/F12 with B27 supplement.
Add N2 supplement to the mixture.
Combine HEPES and L-glutamine with the mixture.
Pipette Penicillin/streptomycin into the solution.
Prepare RPMI 1640 medium for primitive streak induction.
Add BMP4 at a concentration of 50 ng/mL.
Mix Activin A at a concentration of 100 ng/mL into the medium.
Combine Penicillin/streptomycin with the mixture.
Mix RPMI 1640 for definitive endoderm induction on day 1-2.
Pipette dFBS (0.2%) into the medium.
Add Activin A at a concentration of 100 ng/mL to the mixture.
Combine Penicillin/streptomycin with the solution.
Prepare RPMI 1640 for definitive endoderm induction on day 2-3.
Mix in dFBS (2.0%) into the medium.
Add Activin A at a concentration of 100 ng/mL to the mixture.
Combine Penicillin/streptomycin with the solution.
Mix Gut Growth Medium for anterior gut cell induction from day 3-7.
Pipette FGF4 at a concentration of 500 ng/mL into the medium.
Add CHIR99021 at a concentration of 2 µM to the mixture.
Combine Noggin at a concentration of 200 ng/mL with the solution.
Prepare Gut Growth Medium for posterior gut cell induction from day 3-7.
Mix in FGF4 at a concentration of 500 ng/mL into the medium.
Pipette CHIR99021 at a concentration of 3 µM into the mixture.
Dissolve Matrigel in ice-cold DMEM/F12 at a 1:30 dilution to coat an entire well of culture plate.
Culture the cells in an incubator with 5% CO2 at 37°C.
Change the culture medium at the same hour each day without DPBS wash.
Dissociate colonies of hPSCs by Accutase into single cells and plate the cells with 100,000 - 150,000 cells/cm² in mTeSR1 including 10 µM Y27632 on Matrigel coated tissue culture plate.
Change medium to mTeSR1 without Y27632.
Change medium to the Medium for Primitive streak induction (RPMI 1640 containing Penicillin/streptomycin, 100 ng/mL Activin A and 50 ng/mL BMP4).
Change medium to the Medium for Definitive endoderm induction #1 (RPMI 1640 containing Penicillin/streptomycin, 100 ng/mL Activin A and 0.2% dFBS).
Change medium to Medium for Definitive endoderm induction #2 on Day 2.

For anterior gut cell induction, change medium to the Medium for Anterior gut spheroid induction (Gut growth medium including 200 ng/mL noggin, 500 ng/ml FGF4 and 2 µM CHIR99021) from Day 3-6. Replace the medium every day.

For posterior gut cell induction, change medium to Medium for Posterior gut spheroid induction (Gut growth medium including 500 ng/ml FGF4 and 3 µM CHIR99021) from Day 3-6. Replace the medium every day.
Dissociate each of anterior or posterior gut cells into single cells by incubation with TrypLE Express at 37°C on Day 7, collecting cells separately in 15 mL centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge each tube at 1000 rpm for 3 minutes, remove supernatant, and re-suspend the pellets in Gut growth medium with 10 µM of Y-27632.
Plate anterior or posterior gut cell suspensions on a 96 well round bottom ultra-low attachment plate (Corning Inc.) at density of 10,000 cells/well.
Centrifuge the plate at 1000 rpm for 1 minute to gather cells and incubate at 37°C for 24 hours to form spheroids.
Mix the generated single anterior spheroid and posterior spheroid on a 96 well round bottom ultra-low attachment plate in gut growth medium without Y27632.
Centrifuge the plate at 1000 rpm for 1 minute to gather spheroids.
Incubate the gathered spheroids at 37°C for 24 hours to form fused boundary spheroids (anterior-posterior gut spheroid; A-P spheroids).
Pick up an A-P spheroid into a centrifuge tube by mechanical pipette with wide bore tip using 20-30 µL/spheroid/well.
Resuspend the A-P spheroid in 100% Matrigel (Phenol Red-Free) on ice and plate it on a 24 well tissue culture plate to make a Matrigel drop.
Incubate the drop in a CO₂ incubator at 37°C for 5 minutes.
Flip the plate upside down and incubate for another 5 minutes to prevent spheroid attachment to the bottom.
Add gut growth medium enough to cover the entire drop and culture for 4 days to generate Hepato-biliary-pancreatic organoids (HBPOs).
